A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAPPIE/PIEA work, with readable methods, equations, results and visuals. v2 includes readable Appendices A-F. v1 has no included appendix, although it mentions separate supplementary role descriptions; those unavailable descriptions are not assumed absent from the earlier work.

before.justification: v1 reports original Weibo classification experiments on implicit and mixed emotions, component ablations, propagation sensitivity results and a case study.

after.justification: v2 reports original Weibo/Twitter classification experiments, ablations and reader-feedback simulation outcomes in Tables 1-3, alongside the appendix case analyses.

M1.justification: v1 explicitly distills a ChatGLM teacher into ChatGLM2-6B and represents reader feedback through emotion/reposting probabilities. v2 describes GLM4/Qwen-based agents and replaces the probability vector with generated emotion/comment embeddings compressed through two self-attention stages. The author/role fusion mappings also change. These revise central processing components while retaining the graph propagation and gated classifier.

E1.justification: The original implicit Weibo benchmark is retained as Weibo, with matching class-specific split counts. The mixed explicit/implicit Weibo benchmark is removed. v2 adds English Twitter emotion analysis without following relationships, changing language, platform and available-input coverage.

E2.justification: Within the retained Weibo comparison, v2 removes SPDAug and ACOS and adds Qwen-14B(ft), THOR+Qwen, TOC combined with three LLMs, and DeepSeek-R1. Corresponding ChatGLM/GLM4 and DAGCN+Bert/DAGCN rows match across versions and are retained comparisons. The comparator set is substantially revised independently of the added Twitter benchmark.

E3.justification: v2 introduces paired GLM and Qwen agent/encoder configurations, including a 14B encoder, and Twitter-specific preprocessing and augmentation settings. The reported annotator count changes from two to four. Error-excluded macro-F1 is added; retained error-penalized baseline scores indicate that invalid-output handling is newly explained, not demonstrably newly applied. The propagation sweep drops K=9, while the Weibo split counts, 8:1:1 ratio, batch size and sequence length remain.

E4.justification: The component/view ablations expand to ChatGLM and Qwen variants on both languages, testing component contributions across additional model conditions. The mixed-data robustness comparison is removed and propagation sensitivity results are revised. Appendix F retains the original anger example and RAPPIE/THOR comparison while adding THOR+Qwen and two TOC analyses; these are additional comparisons of the same case.

E5.justification: v1 specifies seeds 7 and 8 for the implicit and mixed datasets, respectively; v2 omits seed values. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's wording that RAPPIE significantly outperforms baselines does not introduce statistical evidence.

E6.justification: The Weibo full-model results are replaced: v1 reports macro-F1/accuracy of 0.493/0.608, whereas v2 reports 0.519/0.617 for RAPPIE(ChatGLM) and 0.433/0.566 for RAPPIE(Qwen), under revised configurations. v2 adds Twitter, new-baseline and simulation results, updates ablations and propagation curves, and removes mixed-dataset scores and ablation accuracy results. The headline 5.4%/3.3% differences in v1 are absolute percentage-point differences; v2's 17.4%/6.5% are relative gains against different comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical feedback and fusion definitions are revised. v2's concatenation projections explicitly accommodate 2d1-dimensional inputs, correcting incompatible matrix dimensions printed for the earlier fusion maps in v1 Equations 3 and 5. The task definition, graph update and classification loss remain essentially unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about reader-informed PIEA and role-aware propagation remain. The dataset contribution is redefined from two Chinese implicit/mixed datasets to Chinese-English datasets spanning linguistic and cultural backgrounds. The conclusion requantifies superiority against the revised comparisons without changing the central novelty claim.

C2.justification: v1 interprets implicit-versus-mixed results as evidence of stronger personalization sensitivity for implicit emotions. v2 replaces this with explanations involving missing Twitter following links and language/culture-dependent GLM/Qwen performance, and argues that scaling alone cannot supply reader-feedback information. New Limitations and Ethics sections acknowledge unaddressed LLM biases, reliance on provider safeguards and potentially misleading generated comments requiring manual verification.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the previously unspecified top-k value of 100, two RTX 3090 GPUs, Qwen embedding dimensions, Twitter data sources and the English filtering lexicon. Appendices C-D supply concrete role descriptions, enriched role texts and role/augmentation prompts absent from the supplied v1 PDF. These substantially improve documentation, although the retained reader-agent P-Tuning statement is not reconciled with the new online-agent description.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion for Qwen2.5, DeepSeek-R1 and TOC, and supplies Liang et al. (2024) for v1's unresolved multi-view citation. The Liao et al. (2024) recommendation reference is removed. The main related-work taxonomy and reader-information novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and results discussion undergo substantial rewriting. Each introductory challenge is integrated with its explanation, and the method gains numbered stages, including five labeled graph-learning components. Dataset construction, baseline descriptions, prompts and case material are reorganized into Appendices A-F. Author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2 are redrawn, and the propagation figure changes from metric-based panels to dataset-based panels. Comparison and ablation tables gain revised row/column structures and reporting annotations. Existing prompts, dataset statistics and case material move and expand; new appendix tables display simulation counts and role texts, with additional augmentation and TOC figures. The overall page layout also changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through concrete role texts and generation prompts, and strengthens applicability evidence through Chinese-English and two-family LLM comparisons. These benefits outweigh losing the mixed-emotion comparison and seed disclosure, but unresolved agent-tuning details and numerical inconsistencies limit the improvement. For example, Table 1 reports Weibo DeepSeek-R1 error-excluded macro-F1 as 0.478, although its seven displayed class scores average approximately 0.446.
